name: electric
note: Rhodes-style tine. NOT fitted to recordings, and it is important not to read it as if it were: no openly-licensed corpus of isolated Rhodes notes was reachable without creating an account, and the FP-30X's own electric-piano voice cannot be recorded until the USB-C-to-USB-B cable arrives. The MuseScore_General electric piano was checked and rejected as a source: its pp, mf and ff spectra are bit-identical, so it carries one velocity layer and no velocity-to-timbre information at all, and its partials are harmonic to within 0.5%, so it has no bell partial to measure. bell_partial is the one number here with an outside authority: 6.267 is the second transverse mode of a clamped-free bar, (2.988/1.194)^2, which is what a tine is. Everything else is a first guess. The pedal and damper terms are shared with the acoustic preset so that a change to the damper law applies to both.
